//: Targets the HTTPS endpoint, not http://localhost:5150.
The API calls UseHttpsRedirection, so a plain-http call to :5150 comes back as a 307
to https://localhost:7150. The browser then treats that as a cross-origin hop from
:4200 and the request fails as a network error - which surfaces in the UI as 'Cannot
reach the server' even though the API is running perfectly.
The session cookie is also CookieSecurePolicy.Always, so it would never be stored off
a plain-http response anyway. Browsers treat localhost as a secure context, so a
Secure cookie proxied to http://localhost:4200 is still accepted.
secure:false accepts the ASP.NET Core self-signed development certificate. It applies
only to this dev-server hop and ships nowhere near production, where the client is
served from the API's own origin and no proxy exists at all.
